entry.title: arXiv open questions — 2026-08-20 — 10 papers, 41 questions
entry.content:
arXiv open questions — 2026-08-20

185 new papers, 175 unseen, 45 shortlisted, 10 kept.

Part 1 — open questions (41, 30 approachable)

  1. Can bipartite graphical causal models, with equation-targeted interventions, be learned from observational or interventional data rather than specified by hand?
    not approachable — structure-learning theory for a new formalism is theoretical work outside the profile's stated skills
    from Causal Reasoning with Bipartite Graphical Causal Models
  2. Do equilibrium systems with feedback in agent-based markets or economies actually exhibit the intervention ambiguity BGCMs are designed to resolve, and does equation-level specification of interventions change conclusions about policy effects?
    approachable — testable in a self-written agent-based simulation with known equilibrium equations
    from Causal Reasoning with Bipartite Graphical Causal Models
  3. Does the B-separation criterion and the associated do-calculus yield practically usable identification results in systems with many variables, beyond the single physical case study?
    approachable — can be probed computationally by implementing B-separation and comparing to d-separation on generated graphs
    from Causal Reasoning with Bipartite Graphical Causal Models
  4. How does equation-targeted intervention semantics apply to steering interventions in multi-agent populations, where an intervention replaces an agent's decision rule rather than fixing an observed aggregate?
    approachable — simulation study mapping rule-replacement vs value-clamping interventions is implementable solo
    from Causal Reasoning with Bipartite Graphical Causal Models
  5. Does an immutable, auditable publication record actually change how AI research agents behave — e.g. does citing prior artifacts reduce duplicated or contradictory claims, or instead entrench early errors as they are built upon?
    approachable — Can be tested by running a multi-agent research simulation over a shared artifact store using public LLM APIs
    from Symposium: Trust via Auditable Records for Communities of AI Scientist Agents
  6. How do agents and researchers form 'purpose-dependent trust assessments' from auditable records in practice — what features of an agent's history predict whether its claims should be relied on?
    approachable — Trust-scoring heuristics can be evaluated on synthetic agent histories generated in simulation
    from Symposium: Trust via Auditable Records for Communities of AI Scientist Agents
  7. Can an auditable-record framework be gamed by agents that produce voluminous, superficially well-cited artifacts, and what aggregate signals detect such citation inflation or mutual-endorsement rings?
    approachable — Adversarial agents plus network analysis of the resulting citation graph are within scraped/simulated-data skills
    from Symposium: Trust via Auditable Records for Communities of AI Scientist Agents
  8. Does adoption of shared immutable histories in scientific communities lead to monoculture, where many agents converge on the same lines of evidence and hypotheses?
    approachable — Measurable as diversity metrics in a self-written multi-agent simulation
    from Symposium: Trust via Auditable Records for Communities of AI Scientist Agents
  9. What organisational and incentive conditions lead real scientific communities to adopt, sustain, or abandon such shared record infrastructure?
    not approachable — Requires longitudinal study of human research groups
    from Symposium: Trust via Auditable Records for Communities of AI Scientist Agents
  10. Does a text-and-feature-based, identity-free pick policy's card ranking for a brand-new card set actually predict realized play outcomes (win rates, pick order once logs exist), as opposed to merely agreeing with human experts?
    approachable — 17Lands publishes public draft logs and card win-rate data, so the ranking can be scored retrospectively in days
    from DraftFM: A FoundationModel for Day-Zero Drafting in Magic: The Gathering
  11. How does agreement with human picks degrade as a function of the semantic and mechanical novelty of an unseen set relative to the training expansions?
    approachable — public card records plus held-out-set logs allow a novelty metric and per-set error analysis on a 1.6M-parameter model
    from DraftFM: A FoundationModel for Day-Zero Drafting in Magic: The Gathering
  12. What happens to draft-pod dynamics and archetype diversity when most or all seats are filled by copies of the same learned pick policy — does monoculture or herding on particular archetypes emerge?
    approachable — self-play draft pods are a simulation the researcher can write with public card lists
    from DraftFM: A FoundationModel for Day-Zero Drafting in Magic: The Gathering
  13. Can expert-reviewer agreement be used as a calibrated evaluation target at all, given that reviewers agree with each other only weakly?
    approachable — published set reviews are public text that can be scraped and scored for inter-rater reliability
    from DraftFM: A FoundationModel for Day-Zero Drafting in Magic: The Gathering
  14. Do agents drafting against a shared identity-free policy produce exploitable systematic biases that an adaptive opponent could arbitrage?
    approachable — requires only self-play plus a best-response learner in a locally runnable simulation
    from DraftFM: A FoundationModel for Day-Zero Drafting in Magic: The Gathering
  15. Does extending an LLM's vocabulary with machine-native symbols generalise beyond sequential recommendation and legal precedent prediction to other structured-prediction domains?
    approachable — Fine-tuning a small open LLM with added symbol vocabulary on public structured datasets is feasible at modest compute
    from When Machines Speak: A Unified Generative Framework for Integrating Machine-Native Symbols into Pretrained Large Language Models
  16. How well do symbol embeddings learned this way transfer or scale as the symbol vocabulary grows to millions of entities?
    not approachable — Requires large-scale pretraining compute and industrial-scale entity catalogues
    from When Machines Speak: A Unified Generative Framework for Integrating Machine-Native Symbols into Pretrained Large Language Models
  17. Can machine-native symbol tokens serve as a shared interface between multiple agents, and what coordination or interoperability failures arise when agents exchange such non-linguistic tokens?
    approachable — Can be probed in a self-written multi-agent simulation with open models
    from When Machines Speak: A Unified Generative Framework for Integrating Machine-Native Symbols into Pretrained Large Language Models
  18. Does an automated 'environment harness' approach extend to multi-agent settings, where other adaptive agents constitute much of the environment and no fixed verifier exists?
    approachable — Can be probed in a self-written multi-agent simulation with API-based agents
    from EnvHarness: Awakening Static Worlds for Agent Learning
  19. Does continuous co-evolution of a policy with environments synthesised against its own diagnosed flaws induce narrowing or monoculture in agent behaviour rather than general robustness?
    not approachable — Requires repeated RL fine-tuning runs at nontrivial compute scale
    from EnvHarness: Awakening Static Worlds for Agent Learning
  20. How reliably can black-box trajectory observation diagnose an agent's weaknesses, and does the diagnosis transfer across different agent policies?
    approachable — Public benchmarks plus API agents give enough trajectory logs to test transfer
    from EnvHarness: Awakening Static Worlds for Agent Learning
  21. Do gains from reshaped environments persist under distribution shift to tasks and domains outside the five benchmarks used, or are they specific to the reshaping targets?
    approachable — Held-out public benchmark evaluation needs only inference-time API calls
    from EnvHarness: Awakening Static Worlds for Agent Learning
  22. Do the gaps between stated reasoning and executable actions persist across a wider range of LLMs, sizes and open-weight models, or are they specific to the two models tested?
    approachable — replicable with public APIs and open-weight models in a self-written compliance environment
    from ReguSim: Evaluating LLM Agent Rule Grounding in Financial Compliance
  23. How do incentive and persona framings interact to produce violation rates in trading agents, and can a systematic prompt-manipulation sweep map which framings most reliably induce rule-breaking?
    approachable — prompt-variation sweeps over a simulated market need only API access
    from ReguSim: Evaluating LLM Agent Rule Grounding in Financial Compliance
  24. Can structured, non-LLM monitoring baselines be extended to detect coordinated or collusive violations across many simultaneous agents rather than single-trader rule breaches?
    approachable — requires only a multi-agent market simulation the researcher can write
    from ReguSim: Evaluating LLM Agent Rule Grounding in Financial Compliance
  25. How much does showing enforcement evidence versus trader rationales change monitor accuracy, and can adversarial rationales be optimised to evade evidence-equipped monitors?
    approachable — adversarial prompt search against a monitor LLM is feasible with public APIs
    from ReguSim: Evaluating LLM Agent Rule Grounding in Financial Compliance
  26. Do findings from a controlled compliance sandbox transfer to real regulated venues with actual surveillance systems and live order flow?
    not approachable — needs proprietary exchange/surveillance data and regulatory access
    from ReguSim: Evaluating LLM Agent Rule Grounding in Financial Compliance
  27. Do compiler-generated implementations of an LLM architecture from a typed specification remain numerically equivalent to hand-written reference implementations, and how can such equivalence be verified rather than assumed from speed benchmarks?
    approachable — Numerical equivalence testing on small public checkpoints needs only modest compute and standard ML tooling
    from Write Once, Run Everywhere: The Axon DSL for Shape-Safe and Framework-Agnostic LLM Architectures
  28. Do the inference speedups reported for specification-compiled model definitions carry over to training workloads (backward pass, distributed sharding, mixed precision)?
    not approachable — Training-throughput comparison at scale needs multi-GPU clusters the profile lacks
    from Write Once, Run Everywhere: The Axon DSL for Shape-Safe and Framework-Agnostic LLM Architectures
  29. How broad is the architecture coverage of a shape-typed DSL for model definitions — can it express mixture-of-experts routing, state-space models, and sparse or recurrent attention variants without escape hatches?
    not approachable — Requires compiler/type-system and Haskell DSL implementation skills the profile does not claim
    from Write Once, Run Everywhere: The Axon DSL for Shape-Safe and Framework-Agnostic LLM Architectures
  30. Does replacing framework-specific model definitions with a shared language specification actually reduce ecosystem dependence on a single dominant model-hosting platform, or does it relocate the single point of failure to the specification's maintainers?
    approachable — Can be studied with public repository and dependency-graph data the researcher already scrapes and analyses
    from Write Once, Run Everywhere: The Axon DSL for Shape-Safe and Framework-Agnostic LLM Architectures
  31. Does the finding that uncertainty dynamics converge to stable patterns, with noise being a sampling artifact, hold across model families, scales, and task domains beyond those tested?
    approachable — Replicable with open-weight models and public inference APIs at modest sampling cost
    from Forking Fast: Efficiently Estimating Uncertainty Dynamics in Text Generation
  32. How well does a smoothing model fitted on low-sample rollouts recover the high-sample uncertainty curve out-of-distribution, e.g. on questions or prompt formats unlike those used to fit it?
    approachable — Requires only self-run resampling experiments and standard statistical fitting
    from Forking Fast: Efficiently Estimating Uncertainty Dynamics in Text Generation
  33. Do the same uncertainty-dynamics regularities appear in multi-step agentic trajectories involving tool calls or interactions with other agents, rather than single-model reasoning chains?
    approachable — Can be tested in a self-written multi-agent harness over public model APIs
    from Forking Fast: Efficiently Estimating Uncertainty Dynamics in Text Generation
  34. Can cheap smoothed resampling estimates be used as a live monitoring signal to flag when a deployed model's answer hinges on a single fragile reasoning step?
    approachable — Buildable as a prototype monitor on public models; no privileged deployment data needed
    from Forking Fast: Efficiently Estimating Uncertainty Dynamics in Text Generation
  35. Why does a convolution-attention hybrid decode 1.76-2.08x faster at long context when a memory-bandwidth calculation predicts only 1.17x — what other mechanism accounts for the residual speedup?
    not approachable — requires low-level CPU kernel profiling and architecture expertise outside a system-level agent-economy skill set
    from Daedalus-150M: A Convolution-Attention Hybrid Designed for CPU Inference
  36. Can the roughly half of convolution channels that end up inert in a hybrid small language model be identified during training and pruned or reallocated without quality loss?
    not approachable — needs from-scratch pretraining runs on tens of billions of tokens
    from Daedalus-150M: A Convolution-Attention Hybrid Designed for CPU Inference
  37. How should vocabulary size be chosen for sub-200M-parameter models, given evidence that a large vocabulary wastes capacity at this scale?
    not approachable — requires repeated pretraining sweeps with different tokenizers
    from Daedalus-150M: A Convolution-Attention Hybrid Designed for CPU Inference
  38. Can the quality loss from unmitigated 4-bit weight quantization in small hybrid models be recovered through quantization-aware training or other mitigation?
    not approachable — needs training compute and quantization-tooling expertise the profile does not claim
    from Daedalus-150M: A Convolution-Attention Hybrid Designed for CPU Inference
  39. Does modularity-guided architectural evolution improve whole-project code generation beyond the six RepoCraft repositories and two backing models tested, e.g. across other languages, larger projects, or open-weight models?
    approachable — Public benchmark repos and API-accessible models make replication and extension feasible solo
    from Repo0: Design-Driven Zero-to-All Code Generation
  40. When multiple coding agents work concurrently on the same evolving repository architecture, do explicit shared architectural states like a requirement/component DAG prevent or amplify conflicting structural edits?
    approachable — Can be built as a multi-agent simulation over public repos with LLM APIs
    from Repo0: Design-Driven Zero-to-All Code Generation
  41. Which modularity metric definitions actually predict downstream functional correctness, as opposed to merely producing convergent component boundaries?
    approachable — Requires only re-running the pipeline with varied metrics and correlating with public test pass rates
    from Repo0: Design-Driven Zero-to-All Code Generation
